The full dropdown is the "honest map" pattern — a teaser menu makes the reader guess what's behind each section, while showing all 28 pages tells them the true size and shape of the material in one hover. For a project whose pitch is *the whole system is small enough to actually learn*, the nav itself is now evidence: this is everything, and it fits on one screen.

One quiet consequence of the reorder worth knowing: VitePress derives the prev/next footer links from sidebar order, so the guided reading path now flows Core → Advanced Patterns → Performance automatically — someone paging through with the footer arrows gets patterns before benchmarks, which matches how the material actually builds.

And yes — the loop we've settled into is the real speed: change → build (with link validation as a free correctness gate) → scripted screenshot → deploy in about a minute, all in code, all in git. Deployed — and your instinct was almost certainly right. The front page was carrying three perpetual costs that guide pages don't have:

1. **The typewriter loop** — types a line, holds, deletes it, types the next, forever. That's main-thread text mutation and re-layout on a cycle, competing with the menu open.
2. **The `shine` gradient sweep** on the headline — `background-clip: text` with an animated background is one of iOS WebKit's worst cases: it repaints the glyphs every single frame instead of compositing.
